chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Christian who was called as a witness for a testimony, and then he embraced Islam afterwards; is his testimony valid? He said, 'No.'

This is a singular report (khabar shadh) contrary to the many reports we have previously presented, and it is not objected to based on its ruling against the preceding reports, as has become clear in other places. It is possible that it came out as an instance of taqiyya (dissimulation), because that is the opinion of some of the Sunni jurists.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a convert from Christianity valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a Christian's testimony is not valid even after their conversion to Islam, a ruling that stands in contrast to the majority of reports. The commentator identifies this as a singular (shadh) report, suggesting it may reflect the practice of taqiyya or align with the view of some Sunni jurists who require a new testimony for converts.
